_comment: Advisory only. day injects context; it never gates, denies, or rejects an agent action. No hook here may ever emit a blocking decision -- tests/plugin.rs enforces that, and docs/TELOS.md explains why (affordance, not enforcement: crosslink's blocking hooks are the friction this tool exists to avoid repeating).

SessionStart._comment: The ONE hook here that is not a `day hook` invocation, and the only one that cannot be: its whole subject is day being absent, and `day hook missing-binaries` cannot report that `day` is missing because the shell never finds it to ask. Registered first so the install instruction precedes the two hooks that will fail without it. Emits a systemMessage for the human and exits 0 unconditionally -- a missing dependency must not fail a session, which would be the gate telos/affordance-not-enforcement forbids. Silent when both binaries are present. tests/plugin.rs was NARROWED rather than relaxed to permit exactly this path and no other.

Human-facing notice, kept SEPARATE from the context hook above so adding it cannot regress that hook's model-context injection. Emits only a systemMessage (shown to the user, verified live) on a transition or off-sequence finding, and nothing otherwise. Advisory: a systemMessage is a notice, never a decision.

UserPromptSubmit._comment: day's mid-session channel to the MODEL, designed in v0.6 (docs/ROADMAP.md, Situated injection) and wired in v0.7.0-beta.2. Emits plain text on stdout, which UserPromptSubmit adds to the model's context -- and deliberately NO hookSpecificOutput and no decision field, so there is no shape here that could deny a prompt. Two triggers: a state transition (an event, always emitted) and a standing condition that day's report is partial because a declaration could not be read (not an event, so rationed to a bounded cadence -- day#30 found that an always-present rule becomes background, and a periodic re-display is the trigger closest to that failure). Emits nothing when there is nothing to say, so a healthy session sees no injection at all. COST: gated on a 0.03s git fingerprint, not on the 3.0s kan read. When the fingerprint matches what session-start recorded, nothing a path/tag probe reads has moved and this re-displays from the cache without touching kan; when it moves, or when nothing is cached, it pays for the real answer once and re-caches. A missing cache means RECOMPUTE, never all-clear, which is what keeps deleting .day/ a cost in redundant work rather than a change in answer. The first version of this hook called status::compute unconditionally -- 3.03s on every prompt, while this comment claimed otherwise -- which the adversarial review caught and blocked.

_why_no_session_end: day hook session-end exists as a command but is deliberately NOT registered. Only UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion and SessionStart add hook stdout to the MODEL's context; SessionEnd stdout goes to the debug log, so a prompt for the agent registered there would reach nobody. The one mechanism that would deliver text to the model at that moment is Stop's blocking decision, which affordance-not-enforcement forbids. The useful content moved into the SessionStart hook above. CORRECTED (v0.6 harness verification): this reasoning was right about the MODEL and wrong about the HUMAN -- SessionEnd stderr IS shown to the user, so an end-of-session report aimed at a person is achievable and was ruled out by a question nobody asked. Being reconsidered in v0.6 alongside the status line.
